title: Ember and Choir Again
premise: Jude Thackeray has spent thirty years in the valley of Hollowmere, where the dead whisper through the bones they carve and magic cannot cross the boundary stones. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Jude learns the child is a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath Mount Serel—and that the buyer was Jude's own mother, who traded her firstborn's future to buy the valley's silence. To reclaim the child, Jude must leave the only safe place they have ever known, guided by a disgraced court singer named Wren whose voice can open the mountain's doors. In the thirteenth-turn climax, Jude offers their own hearing of the dead as payment, breaking the bargain but losing the whispers forever; they return home deaf to ghosts but surrounded by a found family, having finally chosen love over the duty of silence.
about_author: L. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former funeral-home archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Victorian mourning jewelry before turning to fiction. They write from a converted chapel in the Pacific Northwest, where they claim the acoustics are excellent for listening to things that are not there.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes Hollowmere: boundary stones humming, bone-carving rituals, the dead murmuring through ivory. Jude carves a memorial for a drowned farmer while noting how the valley repels all magic—including their own strange gift's reach beyond its borders. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness, the ache of a life deliberately made small.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Boundary
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the eve of the first moon-turn, a child of about seven appears at Jude's door, barefoot, unafraid, speaking syllables no living tongue should know. The dead go silent when she speaks—the first true quiet Jude has ever known. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by dread; something has crossed what cannot be crossed.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude attempts divination through carved bone to learn the child's origin, but every reading shows the same image: a door beneath a mountain, and a woman's hand signing a contract. The child, whom Jude names Ash, sleeps soundly while the dead scream warnings. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Warden's Summons
chapters.summary: Warden Odile Ferris's POV. The valley's stern keeper confronts Jude: the child is an anomaly that will draw the Undercourt's attention to everyone. She reveals fragments of an old covenant—Hollowmere bought its invisibility at a price paid long ago. Emotional beat: institutional menace; the safety of the many weighed against one small life.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A dying elder confirms the deadline: at the moon's thirteenth turn, the contract matures and Ash's soul belongs wholly to the Undercourt. Jude realizes escape means leaving the valley—the thing they swore never to do. Emotional beat: grief for the self they must abandon.

chapters.title: The Singer in the Stocks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Outside the valley, introduce Wren Alaire, a court singer imprisoned for singing a forbidden note that cracked the Undercourt's throne-room glass. She hears rumor of a soul-child loose in the world and bargains her way free, intending to sell the information—until she sees Ash. Emotional beat: cynicism cracking against unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: Crossing the Stones
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude, Ash, and reluctant neighbor Tam Broadfoot slip past the boundary stones at night. Magic floods back into Jude like cold water—the dead's voices return, louder than ever outside the valley's dampening. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of a wider world.

chapters.title: Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The group travels through lowland villages where Ash's presence makes candles gutter and old ghosts stir. Tam, a gravedigger's son, bonds with Ash over shared silence. Wren teaches them the road's dangers. Emotional beat: found family beginning to knit together around a campfire.

chapters.title: The Market of Unclaimed Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the city of Vell, the party seeks a map of Mount Serel's underways at a black market where souls are pawned. Wren meets her old handler and barely escapes exposure; Jude pawns a carved bone to pay passage. Emotional beat: trust tested by secrets—Wren hides why she really knows the mountain.

chapters.title: Ash Speaks
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ash finally speaks words Jude can understand: fragments revealing she was not born but made—a soul woven from thirteen others, including one that hums a lullaby Jude's mother used to sing. Emotional beat: devastating recognition; this is personal.

chapters.title: Letters Never Burned
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, interleaved with flashback. Jude finds among their mother's effects a ledger of the original bargain: her firstborn's 'hearing' sold to purchase the valley's warding. Jude understands now why the dead never speak of her. Emotional beat: rage and heartbreak entwined; duty revealed as inherited debt.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits she was once the Undercourt's Voice, trained to sing souls out of bodies, and that she fled after refusing an order. She offers to teach Jude the counter-song that can unmake a soul-contract—if Jude will carry her back into the mountain she escaped. Emotional beat: two cowards choosing courage together.

chapters.title: The Ascent of Serel
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The climb up Mount Serel through sleet and haunted switchbacks. Ash grows quieter as the moon waxes toward its thirteenth turn, her edges going translucent. Tam, the ordinary one, becomes the group's stubborn spine. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible; time running out.

chapters.title: Doors of Teeth
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the mountain's mouth stand gates carved from the jaws of ancient kings, opened only by song. Wren sings; the doors demand a price—a memory each. Jude pays the memory of their mother's face. Emotional beat: the cost of entry, willingly borne.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside the Undercourt: a cathedral of stalactites lit by imprisoned fireflies of soul-light, presided over by the Magistrate of Debts. Wren must perform again before the court that once owned her voice. Emotional beat: old trauma resurfacing; performance as survival.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts the Magistrate, who produces the original contract bearing their mother's signature—and offers a cruel alternative: Ash may go free if another soul of equal weight takes her place. Emotional beat: temptation; the easy cruelty of substitution.

chapters.title: What Tam Carried Down
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam secretly attempts to offer himself in Ash's stead, believing his plain life weighs least. Jude stops him mid-oath, and the group fractures over who gets to decide who is expendable. Emotional beat: found family's first real wound; love arguing with itself.

chapters.title: The Counter-Song
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes the contract can be broken not by substitution but by completion: if the seller's heir voluntarily surrenders the gift the contract purchased, the debt dissolves. Jude would lose the dead's voices forever. Rehearsal through the night. Emotional beat: quiet acceptance becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax. Before the assembled court, as the moon reaches its full turn, Jude sings the counter-song with Wren, surrendering their hearing of the dead. The contract burns; Ash solidifies; the Magistrate, bound by his own laws, must release them. The mountain begins to shake. Emotional beat: triumphant loss—giving up the dearest thing to save someone new.

chapters.title: Running Out of the Mountain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Escape sequence as the Undercourt collapses behind them, freed soul-lights streaming upward like reversed snow. Wren nearly stays, tempted by her old throne of song, but Ash takes her hand. Emotional beat: breathless joy; everyone choosing the surface world.

chapters.title: Silence, and Then Ash
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Home again inside the boundary stones, Jude waits for grief over the lost voices—but discovers the silence is not empty. Ash, learning common speech word by word, fills it: stories, questions, off-key songs. Warden Ferris, softened, grants them all leave to stay. Emotional beat: healing; silence transformed from absence into room to grow.

chapters.title: Ember and Choir
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating brief passages. One year later: Jude carves again, now for the living—cradles, door-lintels, a small flute for Ash. Wren teaches music in the village square; Tam plants a garden on the boundary line. On the last page, Jude hears—not the dead, but Ash laughing—and calls it enough. Emotional beat: resolution; love against duty resolved into love as choice.
